# A New Model for Earth Observation: A satellite built for the public good


By Luciano Giesso, VP, Space Systems


Common Space selects Satellogic to build the first community-governed, high-resolution humanitarian satellite.

### Share

When a disaster hits or a conflict escalates, the people closest to it are often the last to see it from above.


Humanitarian responders, journalists, and human rights investigators are usually first on the ground. They need frequent, high-resolution imagery to understand what’s really happening and act with confidence. Too often, that imagery is expensive, restrictively licensed, or out of reach right when and where it matters most.


Common Space is setting out to change that, and we’re proud to help.


Common Space, a nonprofit building an independent, community-governed satellite constellation for the public good, has selected Satellogic to deliver its first high-resolution Earth observation satellite. We will build a NewSat Mark V satellite and manage launch, ground segment, mission operations, and lifetime support for the mission. The satellite is targeted to launch in mid 2027.


**A New Model for Earth Observation**


This satellite represents a different way of thinking about who satellite imagery is for. Its imagery will be collected specifically for humanitarian and public-interest needs. It will be openly licensed, tasked based on community input, and governed together with the people and organizations it serves.


Common Space calls this a club-good model. It treats satellite imagery as shared infrastructure. A single collection can help humanitarians respond to disasters, researchers track disease, journalists verify events, conservationists monitor environmental threats, and human rights investigators preserve evidence.


The model is built around unmet demand that Common Space quantified in its[2026 Impact Report](https://4baffcf2-f126-493a-8af8-da2f17f4516a.filesusr.com/ugd/25ea80_07340c0dd3ed4a4c8b3400a89a9136ba.pdf) . Private-sector organizations will take part through an equitable, paid membership model that helps sustain the infrastructure and expand access for public good. By sharing the infrastructure, its cost, and its value across a growing community, Common Space can scale sustainably to support organizations serving billions of people worldwide.


“Crises aren’t waiting, and neither are we,” said Rhiannan Price, Co-Founder of Common Space. “With Satellogic as our spacecraft partner, we’re moving from vision to orbit and putting high-resolution data into the hands of those who need it most. This isn’t just another satellite. We’re building infrastructure to serve people for years to come.”


**A Community Behind the Mission**


What stands out most about Common Space is the community it has built. It includes some of the largest humanitarian, human rights, research, conservation, journalism, and mapping organizations in the world.


More than 60 organizations have provided letters of support for the mission, including the World Food Programme, Doctors Without Borders, Global Fishing Watch, Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team, Save the Children, Direct Relief, and Catholic Relief Services.


That community helped shape the mission’s requirements, and Common Space chose its spacecraft partner through a competitive request-for-proposals process. It evaluated providers against its technical requirements, community needs, mission alignment, cost, and path to orbit.


**Why This Mission Matters to Us**


At Satellogic, we believe Persistent Global Intelligence shouldn’t be reserved for a few. Common Space shares that belief, and this mission puts our vision of democratized access into practice.


It also builds on work we’ve been doing for years:


- **International Charter Space and Major Disasters** . Since 2021, Satellogic has been an approved data contributor to the Charter, providing high-resolution, high-frequency imagery at no cost to its Authorized Users during disaster activations worldwide.
- **NASA’s Commercial Satellite Data Acquisition (CSDA) program** . Satellogic imagery supports disaster response through CSDA.
- **Research & Science Program** . We provide free imagery to researchers around the world.


Common Space is taking that idea further, with a satellite dedicated entirely to public-interest needs.


**Just the Beginning**


This first satellite is the start of something bigger. Common Space is raising philanthropic capital to build a six-satellite constellation capable of daily high-resolution coverage of priority areas worldwide by 2030. The goal is reliable infrastructure that organizations can build into everyday preparedness, research, decision-making, and response.


We’re honored to be part of that from the start. We look forward to the day this satellite’s first images reach the people working hardest to help others.


To learn more about Common Space, or to explore membership, partnership, or funding, visit[commonspace.world](https://www.commonspace.world/) .

### Luciano Giesso


VP, Space Systems


Luciano Giesso serves as Vice President of Space Systems at Satellogic, where he conducts global sales and business development, building strategic partnerships with national space agencies and defense organizations. He is a global commercial and space industry executive with more than 25 years’ experience in technology & services. Fluent in English, Spanish, French, Portuguese and German, Mr. Giesso holds an Engineer’s Degree from UCA and an MBA from San Andrés University. He has also completed executive programs in Harvard Business School and MIT Sloan School of Management.
